messages.author: e19ea506112fd25b
messages.subject: open-ended survey modeling in stan
parts:
Hi,

I wonder if it is possible to design a survey where the survey open-ended questions are different for group A and group B?  The rationale is that we believe that group A will ignore some open-ended questions (subset A) while group B will ignore other open-ended questions (subset B).  To limit the survey size to make the survey questions more likely to be answered we give group A the survey without subset A and group B the survey without subset B.  Is it possible to analyze such non-balanced survey?

Thank you,
Linas

messages.author: 8aa9b8cc06fdc99c
messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] open-ended survey modeling in stan
parts:
You can give people whatever questions you want --- it's an issue
of what you want to infer from their (non)answers.

It's only safe to do what you're suggesting if the answers from
groups A and B would be the same, which is presumably not the case
if they have different non-responses.

What you need to do is impute the missing data. There
are whole books written on this topic, and others on the list know
this material much better than me.

- Bob

messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] open-ended survey modeling in stan
parts:
Yes, this sort of thing gets done.  You end up with a missing data problem.  One way is to have some overlap in which questions are asked.  See here, for example:
http://www.bls.gov/cex/methwrkshpsplitquestion.pdf
